newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch financial watchdogs cooperate, mull merger.
newsitem.headline: Dutch financial watchdogs cooperate, mull merger.

text.p: The Netherlands' three financial supervisory bodies have increased their cooperation and are mulling the possibility of eventually merging, Dutch newspaper Het Financieele Dagblad said on Saturday.

The Dutch Central Bank, the securities trading watchdog STE and the insurers review board VK are working on a register for directors of financial institutions that would be used to ensure professional standards.
The register, which would be confidential, would also be used to prevent the re-employment of individuals dismissed for misconduct, the paper said.
Het Financieele Dagblad said the results of consultations could be put before parliament by the autumn.

A merger could be the next step, the paper said. Discussions between the three bodies some years ago produced no concrete results. However, Het Financieele Dagblad says a merger is now regarded as a realistic option.
"It is not the organisational form, but the quality of supervision which is the deciding factor," the paper said quoting an unnamed "insider".
